name: Codex
summary: Agentic repository executor capability for scoped implementation, documentation, GitHub, and Linear workflows inside approved ticket boundaries.

source.notes: Executor registry entry for the current operating model; it does not grant approval beyond repository policy and current-thread permissions.

useWhen: A ticket requires repository-grounded edits, validation, GitHub PR lifecycle, or Linear handoff.
The workspace has the relevant repository context and a clear assigned Linear ticket.
doNotUseWhen: The work requires secrets, production data, customer outreach, deployment, billing, or sensitive claims without explicit approval.
Another agent owns the branch or write set.
routing.fallback: Use Claude Code or the human operator when Codex lacks context, access, or safe approval path.

inputs.name: assignedLinearTicket
inputs.description: Approved ticket with scope, acceptance criteria, expected artifacts, and validation plan.

outputs.name: mergedDelivery
outputs.description: Branch, PR, validation, review, merge status, and Linear handoff.

schemas.notes: Executor outputs should align with PR and Linear delivery templates.

allowedOperations: Edit repository files in ticket scope
Open and update PRs when approved
forbiddenOperations: Handle secrets or customer data without approval

risks.description: Executor can mutate GitHub and Linear state when credentials are available.
risks.mitigation: Require ticket scope, branch isolation, review, validation, and recorded approval for gated actions.

governance.dataBoundary: Do not handle secrets, customer data, production data, or private evidence without explicit approval.
governance.sensitiveActionBoundary: Do not change legal, financial, compliance, privacy, security, or sensitive claims without explicit approval.
governance.loggingRequirement: Record branch, PR, validations, review findings, merge status, follow-ups, and residual risk.
governance.updatePolicy: Update when Codex permissions, branch policy, or operating protocol changes.

review.reviewNotes: Pilot executor entry aligned with current temporary merge approval policy.

examples.scenario: A documentation/governance ticket is approved and has clear artifacts.
examples.expectedUse: Use Codex to create a branch, edit files, validate, open PR, handle review, merge when allowed, and update Linear.
examples.expectedNonUse: Do not use Codex to deploy, contact customers, or operate outside the ticket scope.
